text:
incident-bot: ALERT: rapid node NotReady events in inference-pool-eu-west (4 nodes flapping in 12m). paging oncall. severity: high :rotating_light:
devops-bot: paging rachel, tom for oncall response.
rachel: ack. pulling up graphs. which tenant traffic looks worst?
metrics-bot: 5xx rate for /v1/embeddings in eu-west spiked to 9% at 2026-08-02T04:12Z. error clusters originate from inference-pool-eu-west.
tom: kubelet logs show repeated restarts on gpu-eu-04 and gpu-eu-09. journalctl snippet: 
```
Aug 02 04:11:53 gpu-eu-09 kernel: Killed process 4456 (kubelet) total-vm:4100000kB, anon-rss:1980000kB, file-rss:200kB
Aug 02 04:11:53 gpu-eu-09 kernel: oom_reaper: reaped process 4456 (kubelet)
```

anika: serving-runtime pod logs show container OOMs and occasional `CUDA error 2` before container killed. sample: 
```
E0802 04:11:52.000 serve.cc:428] CUDA error 2: out of memory when allocating tensor
W0802 04:11:52.010 serve.cc:500] container exited with code 137
```

rachel: interesting, container OOM then host kubelet OOM. possible memory leak in runtime leading to host pressure. which models are hot?
tom: model-hotlist: atlas-7b, atlas-13b-quant. atlas-13b-quant has seen increased prefetch and cache warming in last deploy.
anika: also seeing many `mmap` entries in `smaps` for serving-runtime processes with huge RSS. suspect large shared mmapped model caches are counted against host memory because of copy-on-write or failing to release after pod restart.
prod-ops: AcmeRetail (tenant T-301) and BetaAnalytics (T-287) report degraded embedding success rates. both are in EU.
rachel: mitigation steps proposed: 1) enable CPU fallback for embeddings for critical tenants, 2) throttle prefetch and disable aggressive mmap caching, 3) cordon flapping nodes and schedule draining after fallback capacity ready, 4) increase kubelet `system-reserved` and `kube-reserved` mem on nodepool, 5) capture kernel vmcore + nv driver state. I'm going to kick those off.
devops-bot: scaling inference-pool-eu-fallback +6 nodes requested. ETA 4m.
metrics-bot: routing change applied for tenants T-301,T-287: embeddings -> cpu-fallback-pool (100%).
anika: applying config patch to serving-runtime: `prefetch.enabled=false` and `cache.max_mmaps=2`. pushing as canary to 10% of pool.
tom: note: draining while containers crash can cause OOM storms as replicas reschedule. ensure fallback nodes ready before draining.
rachel: good call. will wait for fallback nodes.
devops-bot: new nodes registered: gpu-eu-20..gpu-eu-25. health checks passing.
anika: canary config 10% looks stable. memory usage trending down on canary hosts.
prod-ops: early customer impact: error rate down from 9% -> 2.1% in 8m after routing + throttle. still some tail latency spikes.
tom: collecting dmesg + nv driver logs from gpu-eu-09. found repeated `Xid 43` GPU reset entries prior to OOM: 
```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: GPU at 0000:3d:00.0: GPU lockup - switching to failsafe compute mode
[ 12345.678912] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3d:00): 43, PID=21000
```

anika: Xid 43 indicates GPU page fault or virtualization timeout for newer drivers. could be driver + model memory pattern. capturing GPU coredumps with `nvidia-persistenced` core dump enabled.
rachel: next mitigations: 1) cordon gpu-eu-04 and gpu-eu-09 and drain carefully, 2) for nodes with repeated Xid 43, schedule them for kernel/driver debug out-of-band, 3) lower runtime `max_workers` from 24 -> 12 on gpu nodes to reduce concurrent allocations. executing changes.
tom: performing cordon/drain on gpu-eu-09 now. drain command uses `--ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`. monitoring reschedules.
anika: one pod failed to come up on new node due to mismatch of driver feature flags. fallback already routing those requests to CPU so shouldn't impact customers further.
devops-bot: cordon+drain complete for gpu-eu-09. gpu-eu-04 cordoned, drain in progress.
prod-ops: updating customer comms: posting a short advisory to affected tenants: we routed traffic to CPU fallback and applied throttles; will provide RCA.
metrics-bot: rolling-restart job queued to apply `max_workers=12` across inference-pool-eu-west. canary 5% -> 100% over 15m.
tom: collecting `smaps` and `pmap` for crashed serving-runtime PIDs, saving to /incidents/INC-2026-0802-07/artifacts/. also saved `kubectl describe node` and `kubelet` journal.
anika: also saved container heap profiles and `jemalloc` stats from runtime (it uses jemalloc). sending to artifacts.
rachel: infra ask: please open infra PR to bump kubelet reserve settings and increase node memory size for the next nodepool batch. prioritize review.
prod-ops: AcmeRetail thanked us for routing to CPU fallback; asked for ETA on permanent fix. told them we expect a full RCA in 48h and will follow up.
incident-bot: INCIDENT STARTED: INC-2026-0802-07 severity=high owner=rachel start_ts=1830012345
metrics-bot: after throttles + config patch and node scale, 5xxs at 00:02 -> 1.9%, embedding success rate back to 98%.
rachel: handoff notes for tom: current state stable; fallback pool healthy; two nodes cordoned (gpu-eu-04 drained in progress and gpu-eu-09 drained); canary config shows lower memory usage; known hypothesis: mmap'd caches + aggressive prefetch cause host memory pressure combined with occasional GPU resets (Xid 43) -> container restarts -> kubelet OOM. Actions: finish drain of cordoned nodes, attach node cores and driver dumps to incident, run repro in staging with driver v525/v520 and vary prefetch/batch sizes, schedule infra driver rollback test if repro succeeds. Also review kubelet reserve PR. I'll stay for a 20m overlap.
tom: ack, will take over. next update in 1h or on regression.
prod-ops: creating customer follow-up ticket and scheduling RCA meeting.
incident-bot: reminder: scheduled handoff in 20m. next oncall: tom.
rachel: thanks team. leaving a short playbook snippet in docs: when mmap-heavy model caches + Xid GPU resets -> 1) throttle prefetch, 2) route to CPU fallback for critical tenants, 3) scale fallback pool, 4) cordon/drain flapping nodes after fallback ready, 5) collect nv driver + kernel dumps, 6) increase kubelet reserve.
anika: uploading heap profiles and `nvidia-dump` artifacts to incident folder now.
prod-ops: sending final advisory to customers: mitigations in place; monitoring continues; RCA in progress.
tom: taking lead. good handoff. :thumbsup:
